reason: I'll follow the old stars through the encounter first, matching the first goal.
expectation: I expect the stars to pass through the other galaxy with little direct collision, though their paths may change.

alternatives.reason: Bringing the gas clouds together also advances a goal, but I'll follow the stars first.

effect: The stars survived but gravity changed their paths, completing the first goal; the clouds remain.
reaction: The distinction between changing a galaxy's shape and smashing its stars is satisfying.
reason: This is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the gas clouds to interact as they meet, perhaps compressing, though the outcome is uncertain.

effect: The clouds heated and compressed, with some material gathering as radiation carried energy away; both goals are complete.
reaction: The cooling and gathering added a useful detail to the collision.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the old stars was most worthwhile: it clearly distinguished a galaxy changing shape from stars colliding.

leastWorthwhile.text: Bringing the clouds together was the least engaging decision because it was the only offered combination, though its result was informative.

surprise.text: I was struck that a galaxy can lose its shape while almost all its stars pass between those of the other galaxy.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; both directly matched stated goals.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter out of curiosity about what the gathered gas becomes, though the decisions so far were quite straightforward.
